items.prompt: An -O2 benchmark with a visible DynamicCap object reports the same loop time as the static policy. No assembly has been inspected. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: All virtual calls have zero cost on every architecture.
options.why: One equal timing result does not establish a universal dispatch cost, especially if the target may have been devirtualized.

options.text: The compiler ignored -O2 because a virtual method remained in the source.
options.why: Source virtual syntax does not forbid optimization; no evidence of ignored flags was supplied.

options.text: CRTP cannot inline because it uses a base class.
options.why: A statically known CRTP target can be inlined; base-class syntax does not prevent that.

options.text: The timings alone do not isolate virtual-dispatch cost.
options.why: Equal loop times can arise from identical optimized calls, noise or other loop costs. Control selection/flags and inspect generated code before attributing differences.

items.explanation: Equal loop times can arise from identical optimized calls, noise or other loop costs. Control selection/flags and inspect generated code before attributing differences.
